messages:
jessica (CS): Hey team — Escalation from @tanya at Acme Inc. Users reported they still have app access after Okta deprovisioning via SCIM. Customer says groups were removed in Okta but users not removed from roles in our app. Ticket #CS-8831.

 tanya (Customer): confirmed — we removed `acme- contractors` and `acme-temp` groups yesterday around 18:20 UTC. Our audit shows SCIM patch success on our side (Okta returned 200). But in-webapp users still show role=contractor.

 jessica (CS): Thanks. I pulled the SCIM logs — I see a bunch of `PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/{id}` calls around 2027-11-02T18:20:44Z with 200 responses from our API. Here's one sample response from our logs:```json
{"status":"ok","message":"group updated","group": {"id":"grp_9x2","members_count":0}}
```

 mike (SRE): hmm. On the runtime side we have a consumer that processes group->role reconciliations after SCIM events. Looking at the reconciliation job logs around that time:```text
2027-11-02T18:21:10Z reconciler: queued group grp_9x2
2027-11-02T18:21:10Z reconciler: fetch group membership for grp_9x2 -> ok
2027-11-02T18:21:10Z reconciler: apply role mapping for group externalId acme-_contractors -> mapped to role contractor
2027-11-02T18:21:10Z reconciler: no member removals required
```

 devon (IAM): That "no member removals required" line is suspicious. Why would the reconciler think there are still members? Could be an externalId collision — Okta may be sending `externalId` differently (cases/spaces) and our membership lookup is using `group.id` vs `externalId`.

 sanjay (ENG-API): I see two potential issues: 1) SCIM token scopes. Our SCIM patch endpoint was called by a middleware service using an API token with scopes `scim.group:write` but NOT `scim.user:read`. If the reconciler needs to fetch user membership via SCIM User endpoints, it might have gotten a 403 and silently continued. 2) We historically used `group.externalId` as the canonical key but some Okta connectors post `displayName` only. So our reconciler may have skipped membership removals because the membership fetch returned empty or errored.

 jessica (CS): Is there trace evidence of 403s around that timeframe?

 mike (SRE): Searching proxy logs for 18:20-18:25 shows repeated 403 responses to `GET /scim/v2/Users?filter=membersOf eq "grp_9x2"` from token `svc-okta-sync`. Example log:```text
[18:21:05] svc-okta-sync GET /scim/v2/Users?filter=membersOf eq "grp_9x2" 403 "insufficient_scope"
```

 tanya (Customer): Hmm — our Okta admin verified the integration used the "SCIM Tokens" app and we didn't change scopes. Could the token have rotated?

 devon (IAM): Possible. We recently changed token rotation policy for external connectors and rotated the `svc-okta-sync` token earlier that day. The new token was issued with `scim.group:write` and `scim.group:read` but we accidentally omitted `scim.user:read`. That would explain 403 on user queries while group patch succeeded.

 jessica (CS): So the sequence: Okta removes groups -> SCIM group patch arrives (OK) -> reconciler tries to fetch members using token missing `scim.user:read` -> 403 -> reconciler treats fetch as "no members" or fails open -> role removals not applied. Correct?

 sanjay (ENG-API): Yes. And combined with externalId normalization mismatch (uppercase vs lowercase), even when membership calls succeed later, mapping logic might mis-apply roles. Two orthogonal bugs.

 mike (SRE): Quick repro steps I ran locally: 1) Create group G with externalId `ACME-Contractors` in Okta 2) Add user u@example.com 3) Remove group in Okta 4) Post SCIM PATCH to our API with token lacking `scim.user:read` 5) Observe reconciler logs: `insufficient_scope` and no removal. I captured the reconciler output and partial stack:```text
reconciler: fetch-members failed: 403 insufficient_scope
reconciler: skipping removals due to fetch error
```

 devon (IAM): Long-term fix suggestions: - Fail closed on membership fetch errors (i.e., requeue job and raise visible alert) - Add automated token-scope validation to our connector registry and fail deployments if required scopes missing - Normalize group.externalId on both ends (lowercase trim) and make mapping resilient to duplicates.

 jessica (CS): Short-term remediation for Acme: we can run a bulk deprovision script targeting the affected org that forcibly re-evaluates current SCIM state vs app state and removes orphaned assignments. I can run with CS ops if we get authorization.

 tanya (Customer): Please do. We need removal for ~120 users. Also improved visibility would be great so we can see when the connector token lacks scopes.

 mike (SRE): I'll craft the bulk script. Plan: 1) Fetch current Okta groups via customer's connector using an admin token 2) Fetch current app assignments 3) For each assignment where group no longer exists, revoke role and log reason 4) Post audit event to the org's audit log and DM CS with summary. Will run in dry-run first.

 sanjay (ENG-API): I'll push a small change to the reconciler to requeue on 4xx/5xx from upstream SCIM calls and emit a metric `scim.reconcile.fetch_error{scope=insufficient_scope}`. That will give SRE/alerts telemetry.

 devon (IAM): I'll add a validation check in connector onboarding to assert presence of `scim.user:read` and `scim.group:read/write` scopes and add a Confluence doc snippet for customers to reference.

 jessica (CS): Outcome checklist before closing ticket: - [ ] Run dry-run bulk-remediation and share delta with @tanya - [ ] Run removal after sign-off - [ ] Deploy reconciler requeue + metric patch (sanjay) - [ ] Connector onboarding validation (devon) - [ ] Add alert rule for `scim.reconcile.fetch_error` (mike)

 tanya (Customer): Thanks all. One ask: can the bulk-removal script include a CSV of affected emails so our auditors have a record?

 mike (SRE): Yep. CSV + audit events + retention of raw run logs for 30d. I'll DM you with the dry-run report first.

 scim-bot: Automated note: Bulk job queued by mike (SRE) for org `acme-inc` (dry-run). Job id: brj-20271102-01.

 jessica (CS): Marking this as P1 until remediation completes. I'll update ticket #CS-8831 and loop in legal if audit concerns surface.

 sanjay (ENG-API): Patch pushed to staging for reconciler requeue behavior, tests added for 403 handling. Will schedule canary deploy tomorrow 04:00 UTC.

 devon (IAM): Connector validation doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/scim-connector-scopes (drafted). Please review.

 mike (SRE): Dry-run completed (job brj-20271102-01) -> found 118 orphaned assignments, CSV uploaded to secure S3, shared with @tanya via secure link. No removals performed in dry-run.

 tanya (Customer): Received dry-run CSV, looks correct. Please proceed with removal at 22:00 UTC tonight.

 jessica (CS): Proceeding with scheduled removal. Will post final confirmation here after run. :thumbsup:

 scim-bot: Job brj-20271102-01 executed (live run) by mike (SRE). 118 assignments revoked. Audit events created.

 tanya (Customer): Confirmed — access cleaned up. Thanks everyone.

 jessica (CS): Closing loop: we've updated onboarding validation, reconciler requeue behavior, and created the alert. Follow-ups: normalize externalId migration task (devon).

 mike (SRE): Added alert chart to SRE dashboard and an incident postmortem stub.

 jessica (CS): Great work. Closing thread.
